meta.title: Aleix Casas — Full Stack Software Engineer
meta.description: Full Stack Software Engineer in Barcelona. I build and operate systems that have to hold up: Python/Django over PostgreSQL, Angular front ends, LLM features in production, and Kubernetes on GCP.

hero.intro: I build and operate systems that have to hold up. Three years in the product team of a SaaS analytics platform: Django REST APIs over PostgreSQL holding tens of millions of records, generative AI shipped to production, and services running on Kubernetes. MSc in Software Development & Architecture, La Salle (URL), 2026.

about.title: About me
paragraphs: I work in a team of three, which means I own what I ship: the design decisions, the delivery and the consequences. It taught me early that the interesting part of a feature is rarely the code — it's the schema underneath it and what happens when the data grows.

Most of my time goes into backend and data: Django REST APIs, PostgreSQL, query plans, indexes and moving expensive work off the critical path. The other part is the front end — Angular, and the migration of a whole codebase to signal-based reactivity. Recently I've spent it on the parts that only show up under load — connection pooling, backpressure, autoscaling that does what you think it does — and on getting an LLM to do something genuinely useful inside a product.

I've just finished an MSc in Software Development & Architecture at La Salle (URL). I'm interested in systems that have to hold up: data design, performance, and decisions that still make sense two years later.

jobs.summary: IDDIGO, a SaaS urban analytics platform tracking over 1,000 performance indicators for cities and territories. I work in a product team of three engineers, which means owning what I ship end to end.
points: Built the platform's AI report generation from scratch: the layer that gathers and structures the full data context, plus the call to Google Gemini. What users previously wrote by hand now takes seconds.
Converted the Angular application into a component embeddable in third-party websites, which required a new authentication system. Live in production.
Migrated the frontend from imperative to reactive Angular (signal-based state, modern syntax) and built the testing system from zero on a codebase that had none.
Django REST APIs over PostgreSQL holding tens of millions of records; cut the heaviest endpoints from several seconds to under one through query and index optimisation.
Mentored two junior developers through code review, pairing and technical growth plans.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Most of what I build lives behind a login or belongs to a client, so these are written up as case studies rather than repository links: what the problem was, what I decided, and what came out of it.

items.name: Vista Flota
items.imageAlt: Vista Flota operator dashboard showing 2,500 trucks on a live map with fleet KPIs
items.summary: A real-time IoT fleet platform: a device on each truck publishes telemetry over MQTT — position, speed, fuel — which the platform ingests, deduplicates and turns into live fleet state, trips and alerts on an operator dashboard, archiving the full history for route reconstruction.
highlights: The requirement was 1,000 events/s sustained with zero message loss. The baseline architecture died of OOM at 80.

Removed bottlenecks one at a time — measure, diagnose, fix, re-validate — with Prometheus and Grafana: deduplication moved out of PostgreSQL into Redis, PgBouncer multiplexing 200 client connections over 20 real ones, watermark-based backpressure, MQTT QoS 1, and KEDA replaced by HPA once profiling proved the pods were CPU-bound.
Final result: 5,000 events/s at peak, 3,200 sustained, 0.00% loss.
items.note: Team project across three areas (Application, Infrastructure, IoT). I owned the Application area. Repository is private.

gallery.alt: High-level architecture diagram: onboard agent and simulator publish to an event bus, an event processor writes to real-time state, fleet data and historical telemetry, and a query API serves the operator dashboard
gallery.caption: Architecture: MQTT ingestion, event processor, polyglot persistence and the query API behind the dashboard.

gallery.alt: Grafana dashboards embedded in the app: MQTT pipeline throughput, processor replicas, in-memory queue depth and processing latency percentiles
gallery.caption: The observability that made the tuning possible: published vs received vs processed, queue depth per pod and p50/p95/p99 latency.

gallery.alt: Trip detail view replaying a completed route on a map with distance, duration and average fuel consumption
gallery.caption: Trip replay reconstructed from the historical telemetry archive.

items.name: AI report generation
items.tagline: Hours of manual writing, down to seconds
items.summary: IDDIGO tracks over 1,000 indicators per territory, but reading them and turning them into a written analysis was manual work for the client. I designed and built from scratch the feature that does it automatically.
highlights: The interesting part isn't the API call — it's deciding what context goes into the prompt and what stays out, and keeping that decision cheap and bounded as the indicator catalogue grows.
Built the layer that gathers and structures the platform's full data context, then calls Google Gemini to produce the report.
What users previously had to write by hand is now generated in seconds.

items.name: Embeddable widget
items.tagline: The same product, running inside someone else's site
items.summary: A business constraint — clients wanted IDDIGO inside their own websites — that turned into an architecture problem: how do you embed a full application in a third-party domain without duplicating the product?
highlights: Converted the Angular application into a component embeddable in third-party sites.
Required rebuilding authentication from the ground up to work under a domain we don't control.
